correctness.rationale: The exact right complement w↦w⁻¹c squares to rotation by conjugation and reverses refinement. Independent enumeration reproduced order ten, the 40/150/125 simplices of the proper part, the 315/1050/750 subdivided simplices and the 36/110/75 actual orbit cells. In a flag of nonempty faces the face sizes strictly increase, so a stabilizer fixes each flag vertex and hence the whole simplex, not just the orbit of its interior. Its quotient attaching maps are obtained by taking the orbits of its boundary flags, with the face-size orientation retained. Contracting a 35-edge spanning tree is a homotopy equivalence of CW complexes. For a relator containing a generator just once, cyclically start there; the boundary of that 2-cell traverses the corresponding open loop edge once and otherwise lies in the graph of other loops. The subcomplex consisting of that graph and the chosen pair retracts up to homotopy onto the graph; the other 2-cells attach by the transported maps, precisely substitution and free reduction. Thus this operation preserves the presentation complex's homotopy type, not just its fundamental group. The independent flag/word replay made 74 such eliminations and left [71,71,71,71,71] in its indexing, one loop and one 2-cell. The end model has cellular differential multiplication by five and fundamental group C5, proving the exact ordinary geometric quotient claim. It is not a free-action or homotopy-orbit assertion.

value.rationale: The full Kreweras action is a natural nonfree order symmetry on the classical proper complex, and here the exact ordinary quotient distinguishes it both from the rotation subgroup, whose quotient has two extra spheres, and the dihedral relabeling quotient. A degree-five model supplies actual homotopy data beyond a torsion homology calculation, including usable attaching data and a small test case for other methods studying quotients of noncrossing complexes. The evidence supports this finite exact contribution, not a general theorem in n.
